To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
subjective and objective literacy of rural residents have different influences on financial decisions.
subjective and objective levels of financial literacy affect financial decision making, but the effect varies with the level of financial technology penetration.
Subjective and objective literacy have positive effects in influencing financial market participation, but negative effects in influencing insurance market participation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of subjective and objective financial literacies on financial market participation of rural residents.

the impact of subjective financial literacy, objective financial literacy, financial technology penetration and their interactions on financial market participation, insurance market participation and their mediating and moderating effects.

the influence path of financial literacy on the financial decision making of rural residents and the impact of financial technology penetration on the financial decision-making process of rural residents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the higher level of subjective financial literacy and objective financial literacy of rural households will lead to the higher level of participation in the financial market, and the higher level of financial technology penetration will lead to the stronger impact of financial literacy on financial decision making.
the financial technology penetration will promote the financial literacy, and the financial literacy will in turn promote the financial decision making.

the higher the level of financial literacy, the higher the level financial market participation and the lower insurance market participation, and the higher the level the financial technology penetration, the stronger the impact of financial literacy on financial decision making.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the level of financial literacy and financial technology penetration are both important for the financial well being of rural residents.

the financial literacy of rural households has a significant positive impact on the financial decision-making of rural households, and this impact is more significant in areas with high financial technology penetration.
financial technology penetration can promote the financial well-being of rural residents by promoting the financial literacy and improving the financial decision making.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the financial literacy of rural population is low, and the financial technology penetration in the rural area is also low.

policymakers should pay attention to the impact of financial technology penetration on rural residents' financial literacy and financial decision-making, and should strengthen the financial literacy of rural financial market and insurance consumers.
financial literacy can be a useful policy tool for policymakers to increase financial market participation and reduce insurance market participation.
